name: Silver Ticket Attack (Rubeus)
description: Forge a TGS (Silver Ticket) for a specific service using the service account's NTLM hash. Bypasses KDC entirely — more stealthy than golden tickets.

steps.label: Get service account hash via DCSync

recommended.note: Get service account hash via DCSync
Golden ticket for broader domain-wide access
Use the forged service ticket (HTTP/WSMAN) to move laterally to the target host

notes: Silver tickets never contact KDC for TGS — no event 4769. Stealthy but limited to specific service. Machine$ accounts for host/cifs.

defense.why_it_works: Silver Tickets are forged Kerberos service tickets (TGS) signed with the service account's NTLM hash — not the krbtgt hash. The target service validates the ticket using its own key, not by contacting the KDC. A forged silver ticket for CIFS/HOST on a server grants file system or command execution access to that specific server as any user (including DA), without any KDC interaction — making it stealthier than a Golden Ticket.
defense.prerequisites: NTLM hash of the target service account or computer account. Domain SID. Target server FQDN and service SPN. Rubeus /silver or Mimikatz. Network access to the target service.
defense.impact: T1558.002 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Silver Ticket. Access to a specific service on a specific server as any user — DA-equivalent access to that host. Common targets: CIFS (file shares), HOST (full system access), HTTP (web apps), MSSQL. No KDC interaction means traditional Kerberos logging is bypassed.
defense.detection:
Event 4624 (logon) on target server with Kerberos authentication but no corresponding Event 4768/4769 on the DC (silver ticket skips KDC entirely). MDI: 'Suspected Kerberos forged ticket' — detects when authentication arrives without a prior KDC exchange. Sysmon Event 3: network connection from unexpected source using Kerberos to reach a service. PAC validation if enabled on the service (PAC validation contacts DC — would catch forged PACs).
Anomalous Kerberos activity: forged or stolen tickets by correlating malformed fields in logon events, RC4-encrypted TGTs, or TGS requests without corresponding TGT requests; suspicious processes accessing LSASS memory for ticket extraction (DET0522/AN1443).
Suspicious access to SSSD secrets database and Kerberos key material indicating ticket theft or replay; correlate anomalous file access with unusual Kerberos service ticket requests (AN1444).
Forging or replaying Kerberos tickets: monitor Unified Logs for anomalous kinit/klist activity and unusual authentication sequences (AN1445).
defense.artifacts: Event 4624 on target: type 3 Kerberos with no prior 4768 on DC | MDI: forged Kerberos ticket alert | Absence of 4769 on DC for the connection | Target service access logs showing unexpected user access
defense.prevention:
Enable PAC validation on services (requires DC contact for every service authentication — catches forged PACs). Rotate service account passwords regularly. Use gMSA (auto-rotating passwords — forged silver ticket expires when password rotates). MDI deployment. Monitor for Kerberos authentication without prior KDC exchange.
Active Directory Configuration: Reset KRBTGT account password twice (invalidates all golden tickets); rotate every 180 days.
Audit: Scan for insecure Kerberos configurations.
Credential Access Protection: On Linux, use SELinux to protect Kerberos key material.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Enable AES Kerberos encryption instead of RC4.
Password Policies: Service accounts should have 25+ character passwords; use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA).
Privileged Account Management: Limit domain admin to DCs only; restrict service account privileges.
defense.evasion: Silver tickets only work for the specific service on the specific host — more limited than Golden Tickets but much stealthier. No KDC log entries. Use for targeted access rather than broad movement.
defense.misconfiguration: Service accounts have weak/old NTLM hashes (from Kerberoasting). No PAC validation enabled on services. gMSA not used. No monitoring for KDC-bypass authentication patterns.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Service account with stale NTLM hash (Kerberoasted + cracked):
# MSSQL running as svc_sql with password 'Sql2018!' — same hash for 5 years
# Silver ticket for MSSQLSvc/server.corp.local forged → full DB access as DA

# PAC validation disabled (default — services don't validate PAC with DC):
# HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\ValidateKdcPacSignature = 0 (or absent)
defense.secure_config:
# Use gMSA for all service accounts (auto-rotating passwords every 30 days):
New-ADServiceAccount -Name 'svc_sql' -DNSHostName 'sql.corp.local' -ManagedPasswordIntervalInDays 30

# Enable PAC validation (forces DC contact for each auth — catches forged PACs):
# HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\ValidateKdcPacSignature = 1
# Note: performance impact — evaluate per-environment

# Monitor for Kerberos auth without prior KDC exchange:
# MDI: 'Suspected Kerberos forged ticket (silver ticket)' alert — enabled by default

# Rotate compromised service account passwords immediately:
Set-ADAccountPassword svc_sql -Reset -NewPassword (ConvertTo-SecureString (New-Guid) -AsPlainText -Force)
